next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + ISO27001 summary and private deployment checklist (Sara) - target 2026-04-26

action_items: Sara Patel: Send security pack, network wiring guide, Azure/AWS privatelink notes - due 2026-04-26
Diego Morales: Prepare sample terraform snippets for interface endpoints + sample iptables rules - due 2026-04-30

summary: Intro discovery covering Halcyon's requirements for a private VPC deployment of Redwood. Main concerns: data residency in EU, private endpoints vs peering, egress filtering, KMS integration, and audit logs. Redwood AE + SE explained high-level private control plane options and fallbacks. Agreed to share security artifacts, network diagram, and schedule a technical deep dive for peering/firewall rules.
topics: private endpoints vs VPC peering, transit-gateway vs VPC peering preferences, regional constraints (eu-west-1 primary), KMS/HSM key policies, audit logs and retention, latency expectations and burst capacity, pilot scope & success criteria
questions: Can we do privatelink across accounts? How does Redwood handle key management and bring-your-own-key? What level of flow logs and audit detail are available? Can we pin to a dedicated capacity in eu-west-1? What happens if we need cross-region failover?
transcript:
00:00 Sara (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sara, AE on this account. Diego from our SE team is here to walk through the VPC/private link details. Tom, Priya, Ethan — thanks for the time.
00:12 Tom (Halcyon): Yeah thanks, uh we're trying to understand what 'private' really means here. We can't have any public egress for inference traffic and need to keep model telemetry inside EU.
00:27 Diego (Redwood SE): Right, so two primary patterns: VPC peering/transit gateway and private endpoints/privatelink. With privatelink you get interface endpoints in your VPC that talk to our private control plane, minimal route changes. With peering you can do cross-account routing but you manage NACLs and SR-1s — sorry, route tables — oh I meant route tables.
00:49 Priya (Security): When you say private control plane, is anything back to a hosted control plane in us-east? We need the control plane to be locationally restricted for EU data.
01:02 Sara: Good question. We have a private deployment option where the control plane can be placed in the customer's region or run in a customer-managed VPC. There's also a dedicated capacity model in eu-west-1 so we avoid trans-Atlantic flows.
01:17 Ethan: Ok, latency's important. If we pin to dedicated in eu-west-1 what's the expected p50/p95 for short prompt generation — say 512 tokens?
01:30 Diego: On dedicated pools with GPU-backed instances we usually see p50 around 40-70ms per token for small models and p95 under 350ms depending on batching. But that's influenced by KV cache hit rates and batching. Also, if you run in your VPC you'll eliminate public internet hops.
01:50 Tom: We have a bunch of legacy networking: transit gateway with multiple accounts and a squash of NATs. How do we map your endpoints with our transit topology?
02:03 Diego: We recommend interface endpoints in each account/VPC that need to reach Redwood, fronted by endpoint services on our side. Alternatively, we can do VPC peering per account but that grows with N. For transit gateway, you can route to a single hub VPC that holds the endpoint.
02:27 Priya: About KMS — we must BYOK. We can't have keys leaving our environment. Can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
02:35 Sara: Yes, we support bring-your-own-key. In Private deployments the runtime can be configured to use your KMS for model encryption at rest and for decrypting secrets. We'll need to map the IAM policies.
02:48 Ethan: And audit logs? We need detailed request tracing and per-request metadata for SOC2.
02:55 Diego: We expose audit logs to your logging sink (S3/Blob/BigQuery), with token-level metadata and model version used. There's a separate stream for infra metrics in our console. The logs include request id, model, tokens, and route taken but note redaction options exist.
03:14 Tom: What about egress filtering? Our security team wants to control egress destinations and port ranges.
:03:22 Priya: Sorry, just to add — we also have a whitelist of allowed external IPs, no outbound DNS to the open internet.
03:31 Diego: For privatelink the traffic is internal to the AWS fabric so egress is limited. If you need to restrict to specific subnets and enforce firewall rules, you can put the endpoint behind a NVA or firewall in your VPC. If you use dedicated in our infra, you can configure NAT egress to only specific egress proxies. There's also an option to disable external model downloads.
04:00 Sara: Quick qualification — timeline and success criteria?
04:06 Tom: We want a pilot within 4-6 weeks where we route dev traffic, validate latency and cost, and confirm no data leaves EU. If that looks good, we'll expand to prod 3 months later.
04:18 Diego: Ok pilot is doable. For that we'll need CIDR ranges, transit gateway diagram, and a test prompt set.
04:25 Maya (Product): For safety — can your private runtime do model version pinning and rollback? We need deterministic responses for compliance.
04:34 Diego: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollout policies — canary and automatic fallback to smaller model variants. Also, quantization is configurable but we recommend baseline evals before enabling heavy quantization to check quality regression.
04:50 Priya: Any existing customers doing region-locking? We need examples of EU-only private deployments.
04:57 Sara: We do have a few regulated customers in finance and health that run private control planes in EU regions. I'll share redacted references and architecture notes.
05:08 Tom: On networking specifics: what about cross-account privatelink when using shared services? Our accounts are multi-tenant and we'd rather not open peering to every account.
05:20 Diego: You can create an endpoint service in our account and then an interface endpoint in your hub account. From the hub, route to member accounts through TGW attachments. That way you only provision N endpoints. There are limits but we can provide terraform modules to automate.
05:41 Ethan: Limits are a concern — we already hit interface endpoint quotas in another project. Does Redwood support co-locating a small proxy in our hub VPC to multiplex connections?
05:52 Diego: Yes, a small NAT/proxy is recommended for scale and to maintain fewer endpoints. It also simplifies firewall rules and logging into one place.
06:06 Priya: Encryption in transit — is mTLS used between our endpoint and yours?
06:12 Diego: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 with mutual auth for private deployments if you want. For hosted API we use regular TLS and token auth. For private, we can do mTLS and tie certs to your PKI.
06:29 Tom: Any documentation or terraform snippets?
06:33 Sara: We'll send a network wiring guide and terraform examples. Diego will include snippets for endpoint service, endpoint creation, and sample security group rules.
06:42 Ethan: On logging, how granular is the token billing? We want per-tenant breakdown in our billing export.
06:49 Diego: On Private we can segregate usage by token metadata and customer tags. In Dedicated we offer token-level cost breakdowns in the console export. You can also integrate with your internal billing via our usage webhook.
07:04 Priya: Regulatory: we need proof that no model artifacts or logs leave EU. How do you assert that?
07:12 Sara: We can supply attestation matrices, architecture diagrams showing control plane placement, and run an isolated pilot in eu-west-1. For further proof, we can provide an operational runbook and support an on-site audit if needed under NDA.
07:29 Tom: Networking detail — what's the IP range we see from your side? Are you going to provide stable prefixes for firewall whitelists?
07:36 Diego: We can provide egress IPs for Dedicated/private VPC endpoints. For hosted multitenant, IPs may vary. For Private installs in your VPC, egress is under your control.
07:47 Maya: We also care about OS-level vulnerabilities on the runtime hosts. Do you maintain image scanning and CVE patching cadence?
07:54 Diego: Yes, patching and image scanning are part of our standard Private runbook. We'll share the SLA for patch windows and maintenance notices.
08:04 Tom: This is all helpful. Next steps again?
08:08 Sara: I'll send the security pack and the wiring guide by Sunday. Diego will draft terraform samples. Ethan will export the network topologies. We'll schedule a deeper technical workshop for firewall rules.
08:20 Priya: One last question — what happens during failover if eu-west-1 has capacity issues? Do we accept fallbacks to other regions?
08:29 Diego: We have fallback policies. For strict data residency you can configure automatic failure to an isolated standby in eu-west-1 only. If you permit cross-region failover, we can route to eu-central or global but only if your policy allows it.
08:42 Tom: Ok, thanks everyone.
48:00 End of recording (transcript truncated for clarity, full raw available on request).
